samples.evidence: editor.ts, text-editor.ts and text-box-editor.ts all gained `doc.batch(() => { snapshot(); applyListLevelChanges(...); ... })` with long comments claiming "one Cmd+Z would leave the subtree half-moved" without it. samples.summary: The text-box list test only asserts the net result of indent→outdent→indent, never the intermediate states, and never sets the cursor explicitly
samples.evidence: `api.focus(); api.indent(); api.outdent(); api.indent(); api.detach();` then a single `expect(committed.map(b => b.listLevel)).toEqual([1, 2])`. The outdent step is only observed through its composition with the surrounding indents, and the cursor is assumed to default to block 'a' rather than being positioned. Asserting the levels after each step (and setting the caret) would localise a failure instead of leaving three gestures behind one assertion.

verdict.reason: The batch-per-gesture behavior is real in all three editors (editor.ts:3605, text-editor.ts:2703, text-box-editor.ts:1170), each commented as making a multi-block subtree move a single undo unit. I searched for any test asserting that grouping: read editor-tab-bullet.test.ts in full (only listLevel / painted-x assertions; zero undo/history references), every `.indent(`/`.outdent(` call site repo-wide, every `batch` occurrence under packages/docs/test (memory.test.ts, document.test.ts, editor-read-only.test.ts, edit-link-in-place.test.ts — none over indent), the docs undo tests (page-setup, edit-link-in-place, copy-integrity, format-painter, table-cell-style-guard), frontend docs tests (yorkie-doc-store, editor-undo-selection, editor-step-selection-font-size-undo), the slides text-box-editor test (indent is a no-op mock at :91 and a typeof check at :737), and model/list-level.test.ts (no batch/snapshot/undo/history matches). No test presses undo or counts undo steps after indent/outdent anywhere; text-box-editor.test.ts:351 only checks typeof/not.toThrow, and :550-585 asserts committed levels. The seam is plainly testable with the same MemDocStore fixtures — editor-page-setup.test.ts:159 and edit-link-in-place.test.ts:392 count undo steps exactly this way — so a regression dropping or misplacing the batch would ship undetected, leaving a user's Cmd+Z with a half-moved list subtree. Real, untested, user-visible: blocking under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.summary: No test asserts that one indent/outdent gesture is a single undo unit, though wrapping in `doc.batch()` is a headline behavior change of this diff
finding.evidence: Every editor entry point (`editor.ts` indent/outdent, `text-editor.ts` handleTab/handleIndent/handleOutdent, `text-box-editor.ts` indent/outdent) was rewritten to `doc.batch(() => { snapshot(); applyListLevelChanges(...); ... })`, with long comments claiming that without it "one Cmd+Z would leave the subtree half-moved". No test in the diff or in the tree calls `undo()` after an indent/outdent: `editor-tab-bullet.test.ts` only asserts post-edit `listLevel` arrays and painted x; the new text-box test only asserts the final committed blocks; the only undo assertions in docs tests are in `store/memory.test.ts`, `copy-integrity.test.ts`, `edit-link-in-place.test.ts`, `editor-page-setup.test.ts`, none of which touch list levels. So removing the `batch()` wrapper, or moving `snapshot()` back outside it, would not fail any test — the regression the change exists to prevent (half-moved subtree after one undo, and N Yorkie changes per gesture) can ship undetected.

verdict.reason: No test anywhere in the repository asserts that an indent/outdent gesture is a single undo unit. editor-tab-bullet.test.ts (read in full) asserts only post-edit listLevel arrays, marginLeft, and painted x; it never calls undo() and never observes store writes/batches. Repo-wide, only three test files invoke editor .indent()/.outdent() (editor-tab-bullet.test.ts, docs text-box-editor.test.ts, editor-on-cursor-move.test.ts); of these only text-box-editor.test.ts mentions undo, and those references (lines 351-356 type/no-throw, 469, 534-538, 777-802) concern text and fitted-height commits, not list levels — its list hunk at 550-585 asserts only the final committed listLevel array. Frontend Yorkie undo tests exercise insertText/applyStyle/splitBlock, never a list-level gesture; toolbar tests mock indent/outdent as vi.fn(). The batch/undo-unit tests that do exist (memory.test.ts:233-410, document.test.ts:1062-1091) are store/model-seam tests using hand-written store calls, so removing the doc.batch() wrapper from editor.ts indent/outdent (3605/3624) or text-box-editor.ts (1170/1188), or hoisting snapshot() out of it, would fail none of them. The untested behavior is user-visible (one Cmd+Z leaving a subtree half-moved, plus N Yorkie changes per gesture visible to peers), which matches the rubric's 'major' bar for a changed behavior with no meaningful test.
